paper.title: EvoRoute: Experience-Driven Self-Routing LLM Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: An experience-driven continuously self-refining step-level router over heterogeneous LLMs dismantles the agent performance/cost/latency trilemma and improves off-the-shelf agentic systems.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus revised. The load-bearing move replaces a uniform, human-fixed role→model map with treatment differentiated per sub-task step: cheap models on routine steps, strong ones on planning (Fig. 4). This is heterogeneous_decomposition at parent level; sub null because C04 is compression of a trained artifact. son55's adapt_via_conditioning is kept as supporting (partial): each decision is conditioned at inference on retrieved precedent from an experience base built from the system's own executions, with no parameter update. This follows the run convention for experience-store systems (r04a AgentNet, r05b Memento). Its RE checks on conditioning-source coverage and contamination apply directly. son55's primary reframe_as_solvable_object is not retained: routing is already a selection problem, and applying a Pareto filter plus Thompson sampling is re-application of standard machinery, not a recast of an intractable problem into a solvable object (that card's own RE-3). Its RE-1 question is kept as local-4.

G.reason: Opus sides with sol. The changed object (a static, human-fixed role→model map) and its cost/latency consequences are concrete. Router neighbours are named and three are run. But the 'trilemma' is a framing, not a shown impossibility. Neighbours from cascading/cost-aware routing and from experience-memory agents are not differentiated, and the remaining gap is only partly bounded. son55's own reason states the anchor-2 description; its basis for 3 (run router baselines) is evidence, not gap.

M.reason: Opus sides with sol. Record → union retrieval → Pareto filter → NIG-Thompson utility → append is a coherent response to heterogeneous step demands. But the key assumption that a step's value can be estimated from P(τ)·σ_t (whole-task success copied to every step) is weak and untested. Normal/NIG posteriors on bounded or binary outcomes and hand-set utility weights (opus:O05) are not justified. No distinguishing prediction against a static tuned map is offered. son55's own reason lists these weaknesses; reconstructibility belongs to X.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The write/retrieve/select chain, model pool, prices and parameters are specified. The Optimization Phase (opus:O01), the timing of the end-of-trajectory label relative to per-step write-back, few-sample posteriors, store growth, de-duplication and staleness are unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with sol, on a wider basis. The standard benchmark scorers and price-based cost are credible in themselves. But the reported numbers cannot all come from the stated evaluation sets: several Table 1/3 percentages are not k/n on the App. D level sizes (opus:O04), and the text contradicts the table (55.15 vs 58.28; 63.18 vs 63.19, opus:O03). The task-success label source used in the records is unspecified. son55 noted the attainability cells under E.statistics. Here the issue is whether the reported results are what the stated verifier produced, which A2 assigns to measurement. E.statistics stays 1 on its own single-run basis, so there is no double charge.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. There are fixed-model and three router baselines, and four component removals (cold-start K, retrieval facets, Thompson, Pareto). But the ablations are GAIA-L1-only single runs. There is no static tuned map, random routing or frozen-vs-online K control, so the 'self-evolving' part is not isolated. The routers' training data and budget are not described.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with sol. The cold-start store comes from 50 TaskCraft tasks separate from the benchmarks (a real positive). But the central claim is continual self-evolution from environment feedback. The method writes back records that carry task-success labels (opus:O02), and an unspecified Optimization Phase samples several trajectories per task (opus:O01). The paper never says whether either ran on the evaluation streams, i.e. whether gold labels of test items entered K (A2: oracle/true-label feedback → holdout). θ_sim and the utility weights have no stated selection data. With the core protocol unreported, the held-out support for the self-evolution claim is below anchor 2.
search_scope: §§1, 4–5 and Apps. A–E: no test-stream order, frozen-store report, label-access protocol or Optimization-Phase task source.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder). Task counts and a negative architecture result are given; every main and ablation number is a single point estimate with no seeds, intervals or tests; ablation conclusions rest on 53 tasks.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. Cost and delay are primary outcomes for every method, with a price table and a $28.8/3.6 h cold start. But the Optimization Phase, which samples several trajectories per task (opus:O01), has no reported cost, and neither do PredictTools' LLM fallback, embedding calls, or the baseline routers' training budgets. The headline 'up to 80%' saving therefore may exclude part of the method's own budget (A2: an unequal or hidden budget is charged to cost).
